summary: Batch scheduler backlog causing p95/p99 spikes and request timeouts for production streaming
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-11 09:15 UTC Vendora Labs reported intermittent streaming request timeouts and elevated p95/p99 reply latency. Impact: customer-facing chat sessions experienced 10-30% error rate (timeouts) and p99 latency increased from ~450ms to 3-6s, causing user-facing failures and several support escalations. Environment: Hosted Redwood API (prod), regional routing to us-east, model pinned to redwood-7b-v1. Expected: steady p95/p99 under 600ms for this workload. Actual: recurring p95/p99 spikes and 504 timeouts correlated with high continuous-batcher queue depth.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer workload profile (many short prompts, sequence length ~64 tokens) against /v1/generate with model redwood-7b-v1 in us-east
2) Send sustained 120 rps with bursts to 300 rps over 10 minute windows
3) Observe service-level metrics: request latency distribution and continuous-batcher queue depth
4) Reproduce observed behavior: p95/p99 spikes when batcher aggregates many small requests into large batches and KV cache misses appear
logs: 2026-03-11T09:22:10Z [scheduler] warn: continuous_batcher_window expanded to 40ms due to mis-estimated inter-arrival; effective batch_size=128
2026-03-11T09:23:05Z [api-gateway] 504 response returned upstream_timeout after 5s to client_id=vendora-123
metrics_snapshot: Baseline p95=420ms p99=610ms before incident. During spikes p95=1.8s p99=5.6s, error rate (504) increased to 12% for affected routes. Continuous-batcher queue_depth peaked at 320 concurrently on a single serving pod; max_batch_size observed at 256 on several hosts.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: model update or kernel selection caused token-level slowdown — ruled out. Found strong correlation between batcher window expansion and p99 spikes. Sequence profile for Vendora workload is high-frequency short sequences; continuous batcher heuristics expanded batching window when inter-arrival jitter increased (likely due to upstream client burstiness and a transient scheduling delay on a subset of GPU hosts). Larger batches for short sequences increased end-to-end tail latency due to scheduling and KV cache cold misses. Also observed CPU contention on the host handling RPC dispatch leading to delayed batch dispatch. Reproducible in staging by introducing jitter and raising inter-arrival variance. Related evidence: scheduler logs showing adaptive window growth, PRAGMA telemetry showing increased kernel launch latency when batch_size > 128 for this model. Linked to regression in batcher heuristics introduced in INT-3789 (internal change last week).
resolution: Short-term mitigations applied 2026-03-11 11:02 UTC: 1) Locked continuous-batcher max_window_ms to 8ms for enterprise routes and for redwood-7b-v1 in us-east to prevent automatic over-aggregation. 2) Reduced max_batch_size to 96 for affected serving pools. 3) Deployed per-customer low-latency routing for Vendora to non-batched pool while fix rolled out. 4) Increased CPU request for RPC dispatcher on hot-serving hosts. Long-term fix: reverted the aggressive adaptive-window algorithm in INT-3789 and implemented a guardrail to bound batch_size growth for short-sequence-heavy tenants; added a new histogram-based estimator for inter-arrival variance. Patch PR merged and rolled out 2026-03-12 (see related_github_prs). Monitoring: added an automated alert (label: continuous-batching-tail) when batch_size>128 coincides with p99>2s. Customer notified and validated reduction in timeouts; final validation by Vendora completed 2026-03-13.
